bioprojects.title: Mycoplasma bovis PG45, the type strain of the bovine pneumonia pathogen.

attributes.name: type-material
attributes.value: type strain of Mycoplasma agalactiae subsp. bovis

assembly_info.comments:
Mycoplasma bovis type strain PG45 (ATCC 25523) is the international reference strain of Mycoplasma bovis, a bacterial species responsible for widespread respiratory disease, mastitis and arthritis in cattle. Due to the reported abundance of IS elements and other genomic regions acquired by horizontal gene transfer, and to the presence of a known system of antigenic variation involving vsp gene rearrangements, whole genome shotgun sequencing was employed to provides a critical genomic framework for comparison of additional pathogenic isolates. To minimize mutational heterogeneity in the genome sample, DNA template was prepared from an axenic culture propagated from a single colony isolate of the ATCC 25523 culture (designated MU clone A2; phenotype, VspO ON). The genome, comprising a single circular chromosome was sequenced to closure using the Sanger random shotgun method, yielding approximately 8-fold sequence coverage.

The fully assembled chromosome harbors 54 dispersed IS elements, two integrateive conjugative elements, and gene sets known to be transferred by HGT, thus revealing a striking potential for topological plasticity among isolates of this species and its phylogenetic relatives. In addition, two distinct sets of contingency genes underscore a marked capacity for surface protein variation: (i) the known vsp gene family is complete but extensively rearranged compared to genomic configurations previously documented in this strain, and (ii) a heretofore unknown family of 19 dispersed LP contingency genes is identified, each having a homopolymeric tract of G or C residues potentially subject to frameshift variation by indel mutations (15 in the OFF configuration are annotated as authentic frameshifts). These superimposed systems predict the phase variable, and combinatorial, expression of diverse surface proteins. The properties revealed in the clonal genomic population of this type strain will facilitate the comparison of draft genome sequences, and the assignment of the surface phenotypes, of assorted M. bovis isolates. These characteristics are also relevant to the design of strategies to develop effective measures to control this pathogen.

This project was supported by US Department of Agriculture ARS Project 1940-32000-039-08S at the University of Missouri and the Office of Science (BER), U.S. Department of Energy, Grant No. DE-FC02-02ER63453 to the J. Craig Venter Institute.
The annotation was added by the NCBI Prokaryotic Genome Annotation Pipeline (PGAP). Information about PGAP can be found here: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genome/annotation_prok/
